lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thak work, and careful. They've drawn the coast road right down to the fords.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There's Windthorne, circled in red, and my post beside it. They've even counted the tents.

lines.speaker: npc

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Look at this one. I shut it in a jar last night and it's still spinning.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ordinary dust settles. This doesn't, so something out there keeps it moving. The worst of the grit blows in from the Wind-Carved Rocks.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Cole says the sand devils down by the old caravan have grown bigger this season. Thin those out, then go and see what lives in the rocks.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Something in the Wind-Carved Rocks was driving the grit. A dust devil the size of a house. It's gone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Listen. Hear that? They went quiet an hour ago, and I thought a dragon was coming.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It was only the wind dropping. Next time they go quiet, it'll mean something again.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here. Half the hamlet put something in. They sleep better when the pen does.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good pelts, hardly a hole in them. They'll go to Fred in the morning.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Now, Marta's been odd all week. She says something drinks at the well after dark, and she's been sitting up with a lamp. Go and ask her about it, would you? She won't tell me. She says I'll only worry.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Nell sent you. Of course she did.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It's a jackal, but not like the ones you've been killing. He's big as a calf, gray all over, with one ear torn half off. The diggers call him Old Scrag.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: He comes up from a den south of the scrapyard and drinks my bucket dry. The last time I chased him off, he didn't run. He stood there and looked at me.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Put him down, please. Nell won't believe he's gone without proof, so take her his ear.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's Scrag's ear? Marta sat up every night with a lamp over him and never told me what it was.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: She'll sleep now, and so will I. Here's your pay. The pelts covered some of it.

quests.name: Jerky Weather
quests.lore: Nell Parrish wants her smoker full before the wind turns, and Marta Quill has been sitting up at night over the dry well.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So that's where my goods go. Kesh takes them, Varra sells them, and they split the coin.

lines.speaker: npc

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'll send word to the Agauton post. They'll want to watch that road.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: With Kesh gone, the raiders will think twice about coming this far west. Take this. Fred put in his share.

lines.text: The stamp on this chit and on the tokens is a Thak paymaster's mark. I've had their coin across my counter. It's heavy and badly struck, and nobody out here mints it but the Thak.

lines.text: Good plates. That's the sides done.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The front is the problem. That's where the arrows land, and a small plate cracks there. You want one piece as wide as the wagon.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Pit Mother in the middle hollow at the Antlion Pits has a back like that. I know it's a lot to ask.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'll get these on the fire now. No, look at the color. It's the same as the last batch, and the last batch did nothing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sandmaw's poison is not like the young ones'. My mother used to say only Mother Sedge in Windthorne could cure an old one's sting, and she needed the old one's own sting to do it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Kill Sandmaw and take his stinger to Sedge. Please be quick.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Barthrone boy? I heard. Give it here, and mind the barb.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: An old one's poison is his own. Nothing touches it but what's in his sting. Sit down and don't touch anything.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There. One flask, and that's all there is. Get it to Agauton. Half now and half at sundown, tell her.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Half now and half at sundown. I'll sit with him.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: If Sedge says this will do it, I believe her. Take this. It isn't enough for what you did, but it's what we have.

quests.name: Sandmaw
quests.lore: Sandmaw, the old rock scorpion of the Scorpion Pits, stung Layla Barthrone's son, and her antivenom won't touch it.
quests.completionMessage: If Sedge says this will do it, I believe her. Take this. It isn't enough for what you did, but it's what we have.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Orders. Muster at the court and wait for the word. That's an army forming.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I mean to stop it before it marches. Your pay. Stay close to town.

quests.name: The Gossamer Muster
quests.lore: Gossamer knights are gathering in the Walnut Deep. Captain Maren Holt wants to know who gives them their orders.
quests.completionMessage: I mean to stop it before it marches. Your pay. Stay close to town.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It's the same light. It runs through the velvet the way it ran through the wings.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So it isn't only the moths. The same light is in the deer, and I doubt they're the last of it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The old Summer Court sat in the east Old Wood. Nothing else out there is old enough to do this. Take this, and thank you.

quests.name: The Moonhart's Velvet
quests.lore: Ysolde Fairweather suspects the moonharts by the Moon Glade carry the same light as the luna moths, and wants their velvet to check.
quests.completionMessage: The old Summer Court sat in the east Old Wood. Nothing else out there is old enough to do this. Take this, and thank you.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Captain Holt wants to know what the Summer Queen is.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The last ruler of the old court. The court fell asleep long before Westergarde had a wall, and she slept with it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The light in the moths and the moonharts woke her too. Her court is in the east Old Wood.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: She carries a sigil. Bring that back and nobody can claim the court still has a queen.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Her sigil. The court has no queen now, and the muster has nobody to march for.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The court kept spoils. Take your pick of these.

quests.name: The Summer Court
quests.lore: The fae court is mustering in the east Old Wood under the Summer Queen. Captain Maren Holt means to end it where it starts.
quests.completionMessage: The court kept spoils. Take your pick of these.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Look at the grain. Straight rings, all one width. Wild wood never grows that even.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Someone is growing these briars. Tending them, like a crop.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good work. Your pay.

quests.name: Thorns at the Wall
quests.lore: Briars are creeping through the Lily Fringe toward Westergarde's walls. Captain Maren Holt wants them cut back.
quests.completionMessage: Good work. Your pay.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Steward Vane sent me about your pumpkin rows.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: About time. Look at that row. Every seed dug out one at a time, and every hole filled in after.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A fox digs and runs. Whatever did this tidied up behind itself. I saw silver tails heading northeast before dawn.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's my seed, all right. Now look at the pouches.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every one tied with a knot I couldn't tie if you paid me. You go tell the Steward that.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Foxes that tie knots. I will write that down exactly as you said it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The report goes to Captain Holt in the morning. I suspect she'll want a word with you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Your fee, from the town purse. I have already signed for it.

quests.name: Too Tidy for a Fox
quests.lore: Something digs up Bess Hollin's pumpkin rows at night. Steward Edric Vane needs a culprit he can write down.
quests.completionMessage: Your fee, from the town purse. I have already signed for it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It moves. Very slowly, but every strand leans the same way.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Toward the Overgrown Garden, like a plant leaning toward a window. Something in that garden is drinking the light and spreading it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Steward will want it dealt with. Please be careful.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Briar Heart's core. I will file it under "resolved".

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That is the first forest report this year to earn the word. Your fee, and my thanks, which I write down less often.

quests.name: What Grows in the Garden

quests.completionMessage: That is the first forest report this year to earn the word. Your fee, and my thanks, which I write down less often.

lines.text: Hold it up to the window. See the veins? The light is moving along them, very slowly, from the body out to the edge.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's how sap rises in a stem. Something out there is feeding these moths light.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here, for your trouble. I'll have more questions once I've had these under the lens.

quests.completionMessage: Here, for your trouble. I'll have more questions once I've had these under the lens.

lines.text: Red dragons sleep on their hoards. Years at a time, on the same pile.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: All that while their fire soaks down into what's under them. Gravel, coins, the odd bone. It fuses into lumps that won't melt again in anything I own.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The lumps stick to their bellies. Kill one and pry them off.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: They nest on the Scorched Plains, a long way southeast of here. The little ones are easier, if any dragon is easy. Bring me six.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Six. Some of them are still warm.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ground into the acid, these hold the heat long enough for a stone to set at three carats.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Bring me three gems of one kind at two and a half carats and I'll fuse them into one at three.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ten thousand gold a time. Don't look at me like that. You've met the dragons.

quests.name: Dragon's Hoard
quests.lore: The Dark Witch can fuse gems up to two and a half carats now. Anything bigger needs more heat than her acid holds, and she knows where heat like that builds up.
quests.completionMessage: Bring me your gems at two and a half carats.

stages.text: Bring the Dark Witch 8 gizzard stones from the Ogre Den ogres

objectives.text: Bring the Dark Witch 8 gizzard stones from the Ogre Den ogres
Kill the Ogre Traitor on the Ogre Den's bottom floor
Bring the Dark Witch the Traitor's gizzard stone

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ogres swallow anything that shines. Coins and buckles, and a lot of gravel, because they can't tell the difference.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A stone that rides in an ogre's gut long enough comes out ground smooth and packed hard. That kind holds together in the acid.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There's an ogre den southwest of Binxonia. Bring me eight of those stones.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And the one they call the Traitor, down on the bottom floor. He's swallowed more than the rest of them put together. I want his.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Eight, and his. Look at this one. It's cracked right through and it still won't come apart.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's what I was missing. Bring me three gems of one kind at two carats and I'll fuse them into one at two and a half.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Five thousand gold a time. You know what those stones cost to get.

quests.name: Swallowed Stones
quests.lore: The Dark Witch fuses small gems into bigger ones, but past two carats the new stone cracks as it cools. She knows what would hold it together, and she wants someone else to fetch it.
quests.completionMessage: Bring me your two-carat gems.
